note: PR #103 added the tooling row to IDEAS §7.5 (MCP, CLI, et al.), in the same honest shape as the onboarding row: the surface is present, its standard parts are half-finished. Doc-only.

decisions.question: Is tooling a gap at all, when Nestor already has a 16-verb CLI and a 7-tool MCP server?
decisions.commitment: Yes — the gap is the missing finish, not a missing surface. Present: the nestor CLI, nestor serve (tools/list + call), --json on some verbs. Absent: no --version, no shell completions, --json on some verbs but not all (so a script cannot rely on it), and an MCP server exposing tools only — no resources (the store, ledger, and decision graph are natural read-only resources), no prompts, no published manifest. Mechanical parts tagged open; MCP resources/prompts tagged hypothesis, worth adding only once a consumer needs the store as a resource.
decisions.why: Naming what is present so the gap-list cannot be padded, and splitting open (concrete, cheap) from hypothesis (needs a consumer), is the same discipline as the rest of §7.5. The CLI/MCP split is itself the standard-parts method in miniature — one core, two surfaces — so the gap is the finish on the two that exist, not a third surface.
